data.body: [operator-attested] Criterion: “A defect-seeded duplicate prerequisite build fails the deterministic call-count oracle, and a defect-seeded missing COMMIT still fails the provenance oracle.” This is inherently external mutation evidence because the held-out oracle was intentionally kept outside the fixer-visible/committed tree per rebar-debug. Exact experiment record: `/tmp/rebar_build_count_oracle.py` wrapped the real `python -m build` subprocess boundary and counted successful prerequisite builds with `REBAR_BUILD_COMMIT=abc1234` per pytest worker/session. RED on baseline before fixture repair: the unchanged seven-test module passed its provenance assertions but the oracle failed `expected 1, observed 3`. GREEN after fixture repair: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python /tmp/rebar_build_count_oracle.py` completed with `7 passed` and `observed 1`. Duplicate-build defect mutation: temporarily inserted a second identical `_build_artifacts(...)` call in the session fixture; the same oracle failed `expected 1, observed 2`; restoring the implementation returned `7 passed, observed 1`. Missing-COMMIT defect mutation: copied the shared wheel and rewrote it without `rebar/_build_info/COMMIT`; running the existing public provenance consumer returned RED at `assert _read_wheel_commit(wheel) == "abc1234"`, actual `None`; restoring the original artifact returned GREEN. The final committed fixture behavior is also evidenced by the focused current-main run `7 passed in 18.16s` and Gerrit run 31748823929 success. No wall-clock threshold is part of either oracle.
